name: New Orleans by Night: Kindred and Institutions of Note

pages.name: Jereaux Guilbeau (the Power Behind the Throne)

text.content: Marcel's older brother, Embraced during the Civil War by the Ventrue elder Lothar Constantine after Jereaux was mortally wounded in a Georgia skirmish. Jereaux arranged for Constantine to Embrace Marcel as well, then drove their shared sire out of New Orleans entirely. Posing publicly as Marcel's own sire, Jereaux quietly engineered his brother's rise to the princedom after Doran's assassination and has since all but vanished from Kindred society — but he remains the true power behind Marcel's throne, dealing personally and deniably with any threat his brother reports to him from the family plantation. Most Kindred who suspect his existence at all consider him a rumor.

Embraced by Marcel from a distant, street-hardened cousin in hopes of grooming an heir, Christopher spent his early unlife in open rebellion, disappearing for days and feeding recklessly until Marcel Embraced a second childe, Anthony, specifically to needle him into compliance. Christopher has since settled into sullen, resentful cooperation, and does not realize that he holds enormous unspoken leverage over Marcel's household: he personally saved Anthony and Marie D'Richet from a Setite ambush, a life-boon neither Marcel nor his sire-rival has ever repaid. He is quietly protected by Dutch, the Brujah clan leader, who hopes to eventually see him usurp the throne, and is secretly watched by a Ventrue antitribu of the Sabbat.

A dying AIDS patient Marcel found sleeping in a French Quarter alley and Embraced rather than let waste away, Anthony is gaunt and skeletal even by Kindred standards, but has become Marcel's most trusted lieutenant, running the prince's spy network and much of the city's day-to-day business whenever Marcel is away. Fiercely, unconditionally loyal to his sire, Anthony sees himself as the natural heir to the princedom and considers Christopher's recklessness an ongoing liability to Marcel's reputation.

pages.name: Marie D'Richet (Torpid Prize of the Prince)

text.content: The daughter of a powerful mage, Marie fell in love with Marcel while touring New Orleans but was refused an Embrace by him; she was later Embraced instead by the wandering Tremere Antonio Calbullarshi, drawing a sentence of Final Death from the Hartford chantry that forced her back to New Orleans and into Marcel's protection. Setites ambushed her and Marcel's childe Anthony while they hunted together; both would have died had Christopher not intervened. Anthony recovered, but Marie has remained in unexplained torpor ever since, her body guarded in Marcel's home while he searches for whoever prolonged her condition.

pages.name: Karen Chartry's Household: Josua Cambridge and Julia Cammeron

text.content: Josua Cambridge, a University of New Orleans art student embittered by critical rejection, was Embraced against her will by Julia Cammeron — herself a childe of the Ventrue schemer Karen Chartry, sent to sabotage Josua's career out of jealousy but instead falling captive to his supernatural charisma. Josua's vampiric madness expresses itself through haunting portraits, several of which (including two of his own unnamed sire) went missing after Prince Marcel took him into protective custody; the Kindred of New Orleans watch the city's galleries and museums for their reappearance. Julia, wracked with guilt and infatuation, lives a sequestered existence in Karen's Garden District home, afraid to leave her mentor's protection.

pages.name: The Nosferatu Spy Network: Avery, Roger, and Martin

text.content: The three childer of Lawrence Meeks, raised specifically to staff Doran's (and now Marcel's) spy network. Avery, the eldest, focuses on mortal affairs and quietly protects runaways, mortal and Kindred alike. Martin, the youngest and most gifted, now runs the network and privately suspects Marcel had a hand in Doran's murder, though he has never found proof and feels bound by duty regardless. Roger, embittered at being passed over for leadership in Martin's favor, sells information on the side to Roxy and others, and has been quietly bought off by the operators of an underground Kindred blood auction he stumbled across — he continues to "investigate" the related disappearances while steering suspicion away from the true culprits.

An amnesiac vampire of uncertain clan — he claims Tremere heritage, though some suspect Ventrue or even Giovanni blood — Raymond was manipulated by the New York mage Aaron Carson into running a clandestine auction that kidnaps refugee Kindred entering New Orleans and sells their blood (and, via a captive "breeder," new vampires bred for the purpose) to elders from around the continent. Raymond believes his search for his forgotten past and his clan will eventually be rewarded by Carson; in truth he has been used as a tool for the mage's own obscure revenge against the Kindred who once refused Raymond entry to the city.

pages.name: The Tremere of New Orleans: Nigel Porter, Sebastian Walcott, and Antonio Calbullarshi

text.content: New Orleans' Tremere presence is an unrecognized chantry built from clan outcasts. Antonio Calbullarshi, a 7th-generation Tremere still treated as a wayward child by his clan, Embraced both Nigel Porter (an alchemist he saved from execution by the Council of Seven in Vienna) and, later, Marie D'Richet — the second Embrace earning him a Final Death sentence he still evades by hiding among New Orleans' outcasts, apart from his own childe. Nigel, still not accepted by his clan despite centuries of trying, secretly runs interference for his own troubled childe and nephew, Sebastian Walcott, whose amateur alchemical experiments as a fledgling left him with a drug-induced psychosis and violent depressive episodes. Sebastian is the de facto (but clan-unrecognized) master of New Orleans' chantry, and has made establishing it a matter of desperate personal validation.

A former Army soldier and bounty hunter turned professional vampire hunter, Lanee came to New Orleans in 1985 chasing rumors of a huge Kindred population. She unknowingly acquired several of Josua Cambridge's haunting portraits of local vampires and has used them as hunting guides ever since, destroying at least two of the undead this way. She continues to search for Josua, unaware that her purchase of his art inadvertently spared his life, and remains undetected by New Orleans' Kindred community beyond rumor.

Marcel's mansion doubles as both hospitality and surveillance: visiting dignitaries and problem Kindred alike are invited to stay, letting Marcel watch their movements, indebt them to his generosity, and know exactly where they rest by day. Current permanent residents include Christopher, Anthony, Josua Cambridge, and the torpid Marie D'Richet. Newcomers to the city often use the household's internal tensions as a barometer for reading the city's wider politics.

Formed by Prince Doran in 1841 after crushing an anarch bombing conspiracy, the Council was meant to reward the surviving elders with an advisory role. Membership has been thinned over the decades by an anarch group known as the Phoenix Society, and the survivors — currently Karen Chartry, Dutch, Sebastian Walcott, and Avery — have grown far more interested in accumulating personal power than in genuinely advising Marcel, undermining his decrees and issuing their own "suggestions" behind his back. Notably, neither Morgaine (Toreador) nor Roxy (Gangrel) sit on the Council, a gap that weakens its claim to truly represent the city's Kindred.

A shadowy, deep-cover anarch terror cell responsible for the 1841 City Exchange fire that first prompted Doran's purge of New Orleans' anarchs, the Phoenix Society has spent a century and a half quietly killing Camarilla elders and destabilizing prince after prince across the country in revenge for that repression, with an ultimate goal of eliminating the Justicars themselves. It uses Prince's own pop hit "7" as a calling-card battle anthem, broadcast to warn a city's leadership that a strike is imminent. Marcel knows only two of its members by pseudonym ("the General" and "B"), and suspects covert support from anarchs, Tradition mages, and even the Followers of Set.

Founded in the 1960s in response to Marcel's decree that refugee Kindred could no longer count on indefinite shelter in the city, the Underground Society presents itself as a refugee-aid network but is really Dutch's power base, swelled further by the participation of Marcel's own restless childe Christopher. Refugees who pass through owe favors under the same prestation rules that govern the rest of Kindred society, and Dutch uses this leverage to keep his own political options open.

A cell of five hand-picked mortal and ghoul agents — James "Teddy" Lugor, Lane Nassam, Kendrick McKenin, Miguel Salmararez, and Elzra Taliano — maintained by Gangrel Justicar Xaviar to keep watch over New Orleans' caern and the wider city between his triennial Conclaves. All were once police officers; Lugor (an explosives expert) leads in Xaviar's absence, Nassam liaises with the mortal vampire-hunting task force N.O.S.T.F., and Taliano, a former vampire hunter herself, was personally Blood Bound by Xaviar to secure her loyalty after a failed romance with N.O.S.T.F.'s leader, Detective Carter, soured her on mortal service.

A small, secretive sect based in a house in Arabi, east of the city, dedicated to combating the Followers of Set's smuggling and cargo operations along the docks. Their numbers vary constantly and none make New Orleans their permanent home; they know of many, but not all, of the Setites' operations in the area.

pages.name: The Setite Temple at the Lakeside Hotel

text.content: Hidden in a back room of the shabby, half-abandoned Lakeside Hotel on the southern shore of Lake Pontchartrain, this is the Followers of Set's principal base in New Orleans, run day-to-day by the priestess Manon (though outside Setite elders occasionally assert authority over her). The hotel's owner became a Retainer generations ago after Setite patronage saved the failing property, and the Setites and their Retainers now actively discourage mortal guests to keep the temple concealed behind a front of a struggling small business, funding it through dock-side smuggling of both cargo and Kindred captives. The Followers of Set have also brokered an uneasy truce with the Black Spiral Dancers who lair west of the city.

Three powerful elders in New England, each secretly serving a still more powerful Methuselah, have taken a quiet interest in New Orleans because one of their number sired Lawrence Meeks, the former head of Doran's spy network and now Prince of Baton Rouge. Lawrence was also once a member of the Web, an international Nosferatu intelligence consortium headed by his own grandsire, whose resources he can still call upon. The Methuselahs behind the Triad suspect Gangrel Justicar Xaviar's regular Conclaves in the city mask some larger agenda of his own, and have begun probing New Orleans to find out what it is.

pages.name: Voodoo and the Setites: Marie Laveau

text.content: Voodoo arrived in Louisiana with the slave trade from Africa and Haiti, and the Followers of Set seized control of the practice's Haitian roots early, spreading their influence to New Orleans through the cult hierarchy of Voodoo Queens. Prince Doran's efforts to suppress the cults (including an outright 1782 ban) were undermined by the Setites' own internal schisms until the rise of Marie Laveau, a free mulatto woman who became Queen of one of the city's largest cults in the early 1800s after deposing her predecessor, Sanite Dede, and who for a time genuinely disrupted Setite control of New Orleans' Voodoo practice. Her influence collapsed after her death and the weaker leadership of her successor, Malvina Latour, let the cults fracture again by 1890. Voodoo still exists in smaller, mortal-led groups today, most secretly controlled by a Setite posing as the group's leader; Marcel has recently discovered that local Tradition mages are also involved with the surviving cults.
